output.brief: The jump in write-offs is mostly caused by our own night receiving, not by Haverlow. After the Phase 2 cut (six to four night operatives, week 31), the median time from unload to chamber went from about 44 minutes to nearly 4 hours. Pallets sit in unrefrigerated staging lanes at roughly 15–17°C. Night write-offs rose from 0.6% to 2.9% for every supplier, while day shift stayed flat. Haverlow's trailer data shows product at 2.4–3.5°C when the doors open, so the warm receipt probe readings reflect dock warming, not supplier abuse. The chambers held temperature. Don't raise the chargeback or move volume. Haverlow's complaint is well founded. Restore night receiving staff (or otherwise cut the dock-to-chamber time), set a maximum dock time for chilled pallets with weekly monitoring, and keep the probe check. Part of the rise in Corriebank credits may be looser self-certified claims, but that is unproven. Sample their claims by lot and receiving shift before changing terms. I'm fairly confident in the main finding. The Corriebank share is unresolved.
